text:
Josh Norris scored 35 goals for Ottawa in 2021-22, then spent years fighting injuries, and played 44 games last season. This year he has been in the Buffalo lineup every night, 24 games, but the goals have been slow: 4 goals and 7 points, and none since his two-goal night against Columbus on Nov. 6.

The process is better than the line. He creates 0.79 expected goals per 60 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), a real rate, and the Sabres have scored 9.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That usually swings back. His legs look fine too: top speed in the 94th percentile. The concern is usage. His minutes have slipped to 13.26 a night over his last ten, a modest role for a player Evolving-Hockey had at 1.4 wins above replacement last season, most of it from even-strength offense. Our numbers project about 36 points. If his ice time climbs, the luck has more room to turn.
headline: Josh Norris is healthy, and waiting on goals
